eligible_reason: Not staggered and data not shipped. Study 1 (field DiD) compares 25,000 customers who adopted BNPL within the first four weeks after the retailer's October 2020 introduction with 25,000 Mahalanobis-matched never-adopters. The four-week adoption window is dropped (N = 50,000 customers x 48 weeks = 2,400,000 in Table 5), so Adoption_it = Adopter_i x Post_t with a common post period (the 26 weeks after the window); the AAM footnotes say the Post_t main effect is absorbed by the time FE, and footnote 8 says CSA-type estimators are not used because adopters adopt within the same month. One effective adoption cohort, so not a near-miss either. Purchase incidence is a logit (nonlinear); purchase amount is log-linear OLS with customer and week FE conditional on purchase. Later-adopter cohorts appear only as separate robustness samples in Web Appendix B (each again a single cohort).
design_notes: Field data: weekly customer-level spending at a US apparel retailer, April 2020-April 2021 (22 weeks pre, 30 weeks post introduction). Eq. (1): Y_it = alpha_i + delta_t + beta*Adoption_it, SEs clustered by customer. Table 5: PI logit .778 (.011), N = 2,400,000; PA log-linear .100 (.007), N = 341,052. Table 6 (Eq. 2) adds Adopter x Post x pre-period credit share and basket size (subgroup-by-treatment interactions) plus Post x characteristic terms. Studies 2-4 and supplementary studies 1-3 are online experiments; the package contains only these (jamovi .omv, SPSS .sav/.spv, Qualtrics .qsf, AsPredicted PDFs, PROCESS mediation R scripts).

screener_notes: Abstract flagged DiD; the accepted manuscript shows a single adoption cohort with a common post period after dropping the adoption window, the same construction as Channel Adoption Pathways. Even if weekly adoption dates had been kept, the field data are not shipped.
